A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PDDLLM research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, plots, and robot demonstrations, support reliable comparison despite renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation results for planning success, domain quality, time and token costs, supplementary experiments, and physical robot executions.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds demonstration-quality experiments, a UR5e deployment using a learned policy, and a feature-partition experiment.

M1.justification: The core predicate/action induction and geometric grounding remain, with LoCAS renamed LoCA. v3 adds an execution branch that directly conditions a fine-tuned π0 policy on logical actions, bypassing explicit motion constraints (Sections 5.2, 8, A.1.3). Section 5.1.3 also describes candidate-domain feasibility replacement; parallel predicate prompting itself was already documented in v2 Appendix A.7.

E1.justification: The nine-environment planning benchmark is retained. v3 adds bridge-building scenarios with incomplete or irrelevant demonstration actions and a temperature-based predicate-generation test for boiling milk (Section 7 Q5; Appendix A.10.2). Real-world stacking also extends to UR5e with household tabletop objects (Appendix A.1.3).

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain LLMTAMP, LLMTAMP-FF, LLMTAMP-FR, o1-TAMP, R1-TAMP, Expert, and the RuleAsMem ablation. Their implementation descriptions remain unchanged. π0 is an execution component within PDDLLM, rather than an additional competing planner.

E3.justification: Existing task sampling and planning-time protocols remain. Added experiments vary demonstrated action coverage and temperature partitions of 2, 4, and 100; the new π0 setting uses 200 fine-tuning trajectories. Section 7 also presents Table 3 statistics as predicate-only, whereas v2 reported predicates/actions jointly, although exact percentage denominators remain unspecified.

E4.justification: New Q5 and Table 4 directly test the central dependence on demonstration completeness by progressively supplying pick, stack, and align, then adding irrelevant unstack behavior. Appendix A.10.2 adds partition-granularity sensitivity for predicate generation. These introduce substantive robustness questions beyond the retained prompt-variation, time-limit, and object-count analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report three parallel runs with means and standard errors in Section 6.1. The additional results use the existing uncertainty-reporting style; no new seed disclosure, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds bridge-building success rates of 0.0%, 20.0%, 86.7%, and 83.3% across the four demonstration conditions, plus UR5e execution and partition-generation findings. Under the retained 50-second setting, Expert overall success changes from 93.4±0.1% to 95.7±0.1%, while PDDLLM remains 93.3±0.7%; Expert values also change in Appendix Tables 7–8. Table 3 percentages change alongside the predicate-only reporting scope, so they do not establish comparable domain-quality deterioration. One v3 Table 7 Expert mean is printed as '67.', leaving its intended precision unclear.

T1.justification: Appendix A.10.2 adds a predicate-generation complexity formula summing partition counts raised to feature dimensionality, with a decomposition-based scalability argument. The earlier planning-search complexity discussion is retained through relocation. v3 Section 4 also omits v2's explicit assumption that the demonstration covers the necessary domain knowledge.

C1.justification: The central claims of automatic domain construction from one demonstration and reliable long-horizon planning remain. v3 explicitly extends the novelty claim to domain construction without training data, quantifies the abstract's success-rate advantage as at least 20%, and expands the deployment contribution from two robot platforms to three.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the effects of incomplete and irrelevant demonstrations, argues that excessive partitioning harms predicate interpretability, and adds complex geometry and deformable objects as applicability limitations. The existing missing-predicate failure explanation remains. Conversely, v2's dedicated discussion of generated-domain risks and human oversight in Appendix A.10 is removed.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.12 documents Agilex Pika trajectory capture, CAD-derived object properties, and ArUco object tracking. Appendix A.1.3 identifies π0 and its 200 fine-tuning trajectories, while A.11 explains missing/redundant-element assessment. v2's specific disclosures of 5×5 markers and MoveIt2 are omitted, without establishing that those implementations changed.

R1.justification: The introduction adds substantial positioning relative to VLA models, presenting domain construction as complementary to learned geometric control. New references include π0, OpenVLA, RT-2, CogACT, and Octo; domain-generation discussion also expands through InterPreT, CLIMB, and Oswald et al. (2025). Huang's 2024-to-2025 publication update represents the same prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, problem statement, and motion-planner interface section undergo substantial rewriting. Experimental-design discussion moves from Section 6 to Appendix A.10.1, terminology changes throughout from LoCAS to LoCA, and new refinement and demonstration-quality subsections alter the narrative. The former Broader Impact appendix is removed.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to show simulation verification and explicit constraint transfer. Figure 4 replaces the burger sequence with a montage combining retained tasks and new UR5e stacking; Figure 9 and Tables 4 and 10 are added. Table 3 is transposed, the complexity table moves to Appendix A.10 as Table 11, and the original generalization plot is retained as Figure 10.

improvement.justification: v3 improves evidential coverage by testing the demonstration-completeness assumption that v2 merely stated, and adds a concrete learned-policy deployment and useful demonstration-collection details. The revised method diagram also clarifies the interface. Gains are limited by the qualitative-only VLA evaluation, unexplained Expert-score revisions, and loss of the dedicated deployment-risk discussion. These tradeoffs support a modest overall improvement, without establishing stronger performance for the retained PDDLLM benchmark.
